description: Baseline control run: unmodified main through the exact Stage A harness. Establishes the reference DA / net PnL / p-value that every idea's promotion bar is defined relative to. NOT an idea â€” the fixed measuring stick.
notes: train-eval --fold 77 --seeds 3 --max-epochs 20 --device cuda. Fold 77 pinned for the whole loop. RESOLVED PROMOTION BAR for all ideas (locked): DA >= 0.5009 (=0.4859+0.015, ~2.7x seed std) AND net PnL > 0 AND p < 0.2. Baseline has NO edge: DA below coin-flip, p=0.859 worse than random, -9.29 net over 1484 fee-bleeding trades. Pre-flight (2026-07-08): pytest 257 passed, mypy/ruff clean, GPU idle, push OK.

description: Add absolute time-of-day + day-of-week cyclical features (sin/cos of UTC hour, sin/cos of day-of-week) to the model input, 5 -> 9 features. Within a 1440-candle (24h) window the encoder sees only RELATIVE returns and has no encoding of WHERE in the clock/week the window sits; BTC has real session (US/Asia) and weekend-liquidity seasonality the model cannot derive from returns alone. This is new information, not a re-expression of existing inputs.
promotion_bar: Stage A: DA >= 0.5009 (baseline 0.4859 + 0.015) AND net PnL > 0 AND p < 0.2. Bar locked before training.
notes: Requires decoupling NUM_INPUT_FEATURES (9) from NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS (5, still OHLCV): model.py line-63 assertion (NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS != NUM_INPUT_FEATURES -> raise) must relax to a prefix-subset check, and the vol-conditioned output scale (line ~150, sigma sliced to first NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS). Time features appended AFTER the 5 OHLCV so output dims [0:5] stay OHLCV. Clock features must BYPASS RevIN + vol-scaling: they are bounded [-1,1] already, aren't predicted, and day-of-week is near-constant within a 24h window (tiny std -> RevIN would amplify it toward instability). compute_features gains timestamps arg (5 call sites: eval/train/deploy scripts + benchmark/engine + training_ui/app all already compute feature_ts = validated.timestamps[1:] right after). This decoupling unlocks the whole feature-eng backlog (multi-scale, higher-timeframe, vol-conditioned all add input-only features). RESULT: fails all 3 bar conditions — DA 0.4817 (< 0.5009, below baseline 0.4859), net -7.25 (< 0), p 0.469 (> 0.2). Clock/calendar position gives no directional edge at capped budget on fold 77; less-negative PnL is just fewer trades (1169 vs 1484), not signal. Impl found a 6th coupling point (benchmark/engine.py target-slice). Decoupling (input!=output dims) proven on branch but not merged (ideas branch off main).

unspecced_values.revin_scope: first NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS (OHLCV) only; clock features bypass RevIN and vol-scaling

description: Add multi-scale trailing cumulative close log-return features over {5,15,60,240} minute windows, 5 -> 9 input features. ret_Wm at row t = log(close_t / close_{t-W}) = rolling sum of close_logret over W. The model currently sees 1440 individual 1-min returns and must aggregate momentum itself through the patch encoder; explicit coarse-resolution momentum is a strong inductive bias for the trend/momentum signal (the repo's pre-training-gate baselines lead with momentum). Follows idea-1's rejection of pure calendar position â€” this targets price STRUCTURE, not clock position.
promotion_bar: Stage A: DA >= 0.5009 (baseline 0.4859 + 0.015) AND net PnL > 0 AND p < 0.2. Bar locked before training.
notes: Model change is SIMPLER than idea-1: multi-scale returns are return-like (unbounded, volatility-dependent) so they correctly go THROUGH RevIN over all 9 inputs (revin params sized NUM_INPUT_FEATURES, original) â€” no OHLCV/clock split. Only decoupling needed: relax model.py line-63 assertion to NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS <= NUM_INPUT_FEATURES, and slice the vol-conditioned output sigma to the first NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS (OHLCV) so it matches y_norm. Targets stay OHLCV-only (first NUM_OUTPUT_DIMS) in build_fold_loaders AND benchmark/engine.py (idea-1 found that 6th site). Features must be FORWARD-ONLY (row t uses only closes <= t; log(close_t/close_{t-W})) â€” no leakage. First W-1 rows have incomplete window -> fill 0.0 (neutral, VOL_CHANGE_DEGENERATE_FILL style); those global rows are far before any fold's train_start so harmless. Implementer can reference branch idea-01-timefeatures diff for the decoupling+call-site pattern (5 compute_features call sites take timestamps; here they need OHLCV only, but compute_features already has ohlcv). RESULT: fails all 3 — DA 0.4809 (< 0.5009, below baseline), net -9.50 (<0), p 0.738. Multi-scale momentum gives no edge. KEY: baseline+2 feature ideas all pin DA at ~0.48 on fold 77 (capped) — feature lever is dead (2/2 null); bottleneck is directional-learning structure, not inputs. Idea 3+ switch levers.

unspecced_values.window_choice_reasoning: 5m short-term, 15m=horizon, 60m=1h, 240m=4h â€” spans intraday momentum scales; 4 windows balances coverage vs added params at capped budget

description: Lookback sweep probe: DATA.LOOKBACK 1440 -> 720 (24h -> 12h receptive field, PATCH_SIZE 16 divides 720 = 45 tokens). The specced-but-never-run lookback sweep from the backlog. Tests whether conditioning on a shorter, more recent window sharpens the directional signal vs 1440 minutes of largely-stale history the encoder must wade through. First non-feature lever after 2/2 feature ideas landed at DA ~0.48.
promotion_bar: Stage A: DA >= 0.5009 (baseline 0.4859 + 0.015) AND net PnL > 0 AND p < 0.2. Bar locked before training.
notes: One-constant change (DATA.LOOKBACK). Honestly LOW prior for creating edge (if features didn't move DA, receptive-field length probably won't either) but ~zero implement cost and keeps the GPU busy while idea-4 (directional-loss restructuring) is designed. Sanctioned backlog probe, not a blind hyperparameter nudge â€” receptive field is a distinct structural lever and LOOKBACK in {240,720,1440} is the pre-registered sweep set (DECISIONS search_proposal_policy). Done inline (orchestrator), no Sonnet implementer: trivial diff, no new behavior to test, just keep suite green at 720 (fold literals are _LOOKBACK+_H-derived per horizon-sweep, so they adapt). RESULT: fails all 3 — DA 0.4866 (=baseline 0.4859, <0.5009), net -6.64 (<0), p 0.760. Lookback 720 indistinguishable from baseline; receptive-field lever null (as predicted, low prior). 4 runs now pin DA ~0.48. Features + receptive-field exhausted. Idea 4 = directional-loss (aux head).

description: Auxiliary directional classification head sharing the encoder. A small linear head off the encoder trunk predicts the sign of the final-horizon cumulative close move, trained with BCE against the realized sign, weighted by AUX_DIRECTION_WEIGHT and added to the total loss. The head is DROPPED at inference (model.forward still returns only quantiles; forward_with_direction is training-only), so the bake-off/deploy/benchmark interfaces are untouched. Hypothesis: a direct directional gradient shapes the SHARED encoder to be more directionally informative, which the quantile head expresses through q50's sign -> higher DA. First loss-lever idea, after features(2/2) and lookback all left DA pinned at ~0.48.
promotion_bar: Stage A: DA >= 0.5009 (baseline 0.4859 + 0.015) AND net PnL > 0 AND p < 0.2. Bar locked before training.
notes: Chosen over directly cranking q50 directional pressure because DECISIONS 'loss' history shows that path COLLAPSES median calibration (coverage-penalty weights 1.0/0.1 drove DA->0.49; the pre-final-step direction penalty 'destroyed median calibration'). Aux head sidesteps that: it doesn't force q50's sign, it enriches the shared representation, leaving pinball+coverage to keep quantiles honest. Mechanism is INDIRECT/uncertain (aux head may learn direction without it transferring to q50) — if so, that is itself the informative finding that the median is structurally directionless. Surface: model.py (refactor forward to shared trunk 'flat'; add direction_head = Linear(num_tokens*d_model, 1); add training-only forward_with_direction -> (quantiles, logit); forward(x) UNCHANGED), loss.py (predictor_loss optional direction_logit + aux_weight; label = sign(target_cum final close); F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits; LossComponents +aux field, defaults keep other callers green), training.py (2 call sites use forward_with_direction; accumulate+SSE-log aux), constants.py (AUX_DIRECTION_WEIGHT). CHANGELOG+DECISIONS same commit if a decision value is added (aux head is a new loss structure -> amend DECISIONS 'loss').

unspecced_values.aux_weight_reasoning: BCE term ~0.69 nats; at weight 0.5 it contributes ~0.35 to a total dominated by pinball ~0.11 — strong directional gradient without swamping quantile learning. Starting bet; sweep later if the idea shows life.
unspecced_values.aux_target: final-horizon cumulative close sign only (the traded quantity; avoids noisy near-zero early-step signs)
